title: Quantization Safety & Canary Gatekeeper: Rollout Playbook
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Create an operational playbook and initiative tracker for rolling out quantized model variants with a safety-first canary gatekeeper. The goal is to realize per-token cost savings from int8/int4 profiles while preventing regressions in latency, output quality, and customer-facing errors. This ticket coordinates product, SRE, runtime, and research to define gating metrics, telemetry, and automated rollback criteria for staged releases.
objectives: Define measurable quality and latency gates for canary quantized variants
Standardize a gatekeeper automation that enforces thresholds and triggers rollbacks
Ship an observable dashboard with per-route delta metrics (cost, latency, rerank rate, hallucination signals)
Document operational runbooks and run a multi-customer pilot to validate savings and safety
success_metrics: Aggregate token cost reduction >= 12% for targeted routes in pilot quarter
No customer-visible quality regressions: user-reported error rate delta <= 0.1%
Canary automation reduces mean time-to-rollback to < 5 minutes for failing canaries
Clear per-route signal coverage: latency, token-accuracy proxy, and model divergence logged for 95% of pilot traffic
approach: Phase 0: Define metrics and detection heuristics jointly with Research (proxy checks for semantic drift)
Phase 1: Small internal canary on low-risk routes (5% traffic) running side-by-side baseline + quantized variant for A/B comparison
Phase 2: Gatekeeper automation that evaluates sliding-window metrics and enforces automatic rollback or scale-down
Phase 3: Expand pilot to select paying customers with explicit opt-in and feedback collection
Phase 4: Post-pilot roll, refine quant profiles, and codify as runtime-configurable rollout presets
acceptance_criteria: Gate definitions documented and reviewed by PM, Research, and SRE
Automation implemented that can detect threshold breaches and trigger rollback via existing rollout API
Pilot executed against 3 distinct workload archetypes (short-chat, long-context summarization, embedding-heavy) with baseline comparison results stored
Dashboard with per-route delta metrics available in Console and linked in this ticket
Runbook written with escalation paths and manual override steps
risks: Quality regressions that escape proxy detections (semantic drift not caught by simple heuristics)
Unanticipated latency penalty for long-context workloads due to quant kernel inefficiencies
False positives from noisy telemetry leading to unnecessary rollbacks and customer churn
Dependency on SRE automation capacity and rollout API changes during the pilot window
decisions: Use rollback thresholds based on 10-minute sliding-window aggregated metrics (agreed by SRE)
Start pilot with int8 profile only; reserve int4 experiments for Phase 3 after pilot success
Require manual signoff from Customer Success before enrolling any paying customer into pilot
Telemetry surface must include both absolute and relative metrics to baseline (not just percent change)
